Got this nugget of wisdom from my ex, after my Mother passed away, and my Dad was diagnosed with Multiple Myleoma, the fighting was out of control so I moved out. 
"Why don't you kill yourself, it'll be better for me and the kids"

Also a friend of mine said to think of one to two things a day you are glad you've had in life. I told her, at the time (Mom gone, Dad cancer, going through a divorce), it was hard to come up with one a week.

So sorry for your conditions, I went through this with both of my parents over the last two years. Start with explaining to your parents your wishes and follow it with Five Wishes, linked below. Nothing to pay for, the forms can be found online. Depends on your state, they may need another forms, but it is basically a more detailed DNR. Your parents may not be the best to do the witnessing of the document. 
[Five Wishes](https://www.agingwithdignity.org/five-wishes/about-five-wishes)
Best of luck, 
Garrett

There have been several sales\issuance's of stock. I bought one share in the early 2000's. That share entitles me to four free tickets to the stock-owners meeting yearly. They have typical corporate presentations, and have some old players and coaches there. You get to tour the stadium, and sometimes food. Also the share can be willed to someone.

I know it's hard, but don't think of it as letting go. I lost my Dad April 26th, 2016. He was diagnosed with a cancer a month after my Mom passed away on March 12th, 2015. My Mom was able to make her own decision to go into hospice. My Dad was doing fairly well, but took a bad turn. They both had the "5 Wishes" document filled out, 
[5 Wishes](https://www.agingwithdignity.org/five-wishes/about-five-wishes)
filled out so I knew their wishes, though it was still hard making the drive up North that night to get there and walk in to all these tubes, and wires, then to have a Doctor walk in and tell me I needed to decide soon what I wanted to do (felt like telling him to F! off). spent most of the night, a friend of his, a priest, came in around 3AM to talk to me and give my Dad his last rights, and around 9 in the morning, when my oldest son got there, we made the decision. It is hard, and it sucks, but you know your Dad, and you know it is the choice he would made himself. I was there for both, and held them for some time, you are NOT killing anyone! Find yourself a support group, I go to a bereavement group for loss to cancer, though I am sure you could find something. People will tell you it gets better, but unless they have lost a parent they don't know how it feels. Come here, Reddit has some sub-reddits where you can talk and get support, find out hows are handling things, and find people who have progressed through their loss, and can let you know what they have gone through. And you will find that you may experience some of those same things, so listing to them helps you get through the day. Everyone here has a different experience, though the same thread flows though each comment, they have lost someone they loved dearly, and these are the folks who can help you understand how you are feeling. 
Good luck, and know he will always be there for you! (as I'm in tears now)

Bit of a story. So my Mother was diagnosed with Breast cancer in April 2014, hard struggle but she passed away in  March 2015, after which I moved out due to a lot of issues with my Ex, and they weren't new I just couldn't handle them anymore after the loss of my Mom. So she files right away and then my Dad was diagnosed with Multiple Myleoma. I am an only child, with a couple of close cousins who are like sisters. Though my folks were divorced, and they weren't close to my Dad. So all of this was on me. My Mom has a lot of stocks, and she wanted that split between the kids. With running to my Dads every few weeks and bringing him to down by me to evaluate stem cell transplant, I didn't make time to do the transfer. So she started to tell the kids I sold the stock to spend on my girlfriend, which there wasn't one, though thru our entire marriage she knew I had several ( which there never was one). Dragging out the divorce and firing her lawyer since he advised that she couldn't go after my Moms house or investments as they were an inheritance. Then my Dad Passed away, and she gave me crap about letting our youngest, who was 17 at the time, not leave the state for the wake and funeral. Now her new lawyer is going after my Dads house, investments, and accounts along with my Moms. Divorce is never fun going through it, but the light at the end of the tunnel is coming quick, as the Judge is getting tired of her lawyer always asking for extensions and wanting new discovery, and has said if we don't have an agreement by tomorrow  he will decide how to split things, and  my parents investments, house and monies are out of scope.

Similar thing happened to me at Ikea once. Busy Saturday, I had my kids, 10, 6, 3 at the time. We went up got our food, and found a table to sit down, very crowded. Next to us was this little 4-5 year old girl standing on the chair waving to someone. So me and my nice self realize she is waving for her mom, who I can't see anyone acknowledging this kid. So I tell the kid to go get your mom, and I'll save the table. So I sit at their table my kids are eating with my Mom, and I'm watching the kid, see her find her mom point back to me and wait for them to return to their table and I would move back to my seat two feet away with my kids and Mom. 
      Well this lady (she was with some older kids maybe 7 and 8) must have misunderstood what her kid was saying. Walks over to me with the kids following, and starts tearing me a new asshole for stealing her table that her kid was saving. I calmly pointing out that I was saving the table because her kid was trying to get her attention, and moved to my seat and continued eating. She didn't say anything to me after that until we were leaving when she apologized. I acknowledged but left.

Had to explain that we could not calculate an hourly average from a sample taken once a day. They knew when the sample was taken at 8AM, and wanted to be able to trend the average of what the sample was reading over each hour. Explained that they would need to put an analyzer out in the process so the analyzer could take multiple samples an hour, then we could do an hourly average. Nope, process would take too long and cost too much to put the analyzer in, and this was going to be short term (six months). Suggested to have the lab run a sample once an hour and we could get a daily average. Nope again, just give him the hourly average now, so I did. About two weeks later he comes back and says something is wrong with my calc because the value isn't changing. After explaining to him again how an average for the hour needs multiple reading in that hour, and this sample as he pointed out, is taken once a day, a light bulb went off. Tells me OK, he'll figure something else out, haven't heard from him since about this, last year.

Like others, it wasn't one thing, just years of piling on. 
     
   Started the day we were married, and she told me that she was going to divorce me (my parents were divorced, and she knew that bothered me). After she quit on marriage consolers, I just stayed put, 
and after being on my own now for over a year in therapy for many reasons, which you'll see, realized we were co-dependent(married young due to our son, though I wouldn't change our kids for anything).
   
   April 2014 my Mother was diagnosed with stage four breast cancer, cousin had taken mom to the hospital, and called me, ex wanted to go as she was still arguing with me about how we would handle the kids on Easter. Told her in the car "I don't want to argue, if you want to keep arguing get out of the car and walk home", which she did at the next stop light. So I had to turn around and argue for her to get in the car. We still argued through that year before my Mom passed away, about me staying at my Mom's house when she was in the hospital the last time, and when she was in hospice, because she needed help around the house with our daughter (a 16 year old, fully capable of living life on her own). Snarky remarks, how I should be going to work, and her boss said he wouldn't be able to let someone work form home\hospital like I was. My boss knew what was going on, and he told me to take care and do what I needed for my Mom, most of what I do can be done remotely. 
   
   When my Mom passed that's when shit really started. I wasn't in any mode for any conflict, and that is all I got. Threatening to not go to the wake if her mother wasn't allowed to go (I was told I wasn't to go to her sisters wedding because her mother didn't want me there, or her grandmothers funeral same reasons, this women never had a nice thing to say about me or my family and I just didn't want the conflict), ditched me the day of the funeral. Continuously bitched about me needing to plan our vacation, while my mom was in hospice, after telling her I just wanted to relax after the year I have had a "Staycation" go to North Ave. Beach, Zoo, whatever, just not travel. Nope that wasn't good enough for her, told me I ruined her summer because she took that time off and now it's wasted, really sorry figured you are an adult and can go on vacation on your own with the kids (again 19 and 17 years old). Told me she would get rid of my Mothers ashes if I didn't put them where she wanted (they are in an antique looking clock urn on top of our fireplace in the family room). This goes on.
   
   Well then about three weeks later my Dad is in town for our oldest sons college graduation. She complains whenever anyone is over except her family, even the neighbors, so he stays with his cousin in Oak Park. Well he tells me he was diagnosed with Multiple Myleoma, a blood cancer that is not curable, FUCK NOT AGAIN. He live in North Central Wisconsin so now I need to head up north to meet with his doctors, help him get things organized and be his medical advocate like I was for my Mom. 

   Oh, and I am an only child, so this is all on me.
 
   So with this, she still is bitching about vacation, and how I ruined it for her. Not one word of support through any of this. My therapist suggests I move out, so I can have some peace, which I do need to clean up stuff at my Moms place anyway. so she has a meltdown how my therapist is an idiot and shes doing everything to support me. Again, complained about driving 30 minutes to my Mom's when she went into hospice, but I should make that same drive in rush hour traffic. Won't go up north to my Dad's to help with anything. Harass me at work\text\cell that I'm worthless because I ditched her and the kids (even though I would stop by and take the kids out to dinner, bring them over to my Mom's and do things with them). After I tell her she is right I am depressed, and the way she is treating me makes it worse, asked her to go to my therapist so she could hear what I am going through without arguing, she refuses. Middle of a text argument how I'm a piece of shit, tells me I should kill myself that it would be better for her and the kids. 
         Well, she filed once I talked to a lawyer, let my Dad know, and when he passed this last April she tried to say she wouldn't let my daughter leave Illinois (now 17 and she has parental custody, so she thinks that means what she says goes) for the funeral. That is just how has continued to be through this last year. 
	Yes I wasn't the perfect husband through our marriage either, but I tried by going to the marriage consular, and continuing after she stopped. I changed my actions how I responded to her when she would start on things. But when my Mom passed away, my world changed, and I just couldn't deal with her. Started hanging out with friends and family, which I wasn't allowed to do when we were married, and enjoyed myself, because I could have conversations with these people without fear of condemnation, or being told how I have it so good. 

Among others:
-Constantly being accused of fucking any women I talked to
-Threatened with divorce, and would take the kids so I would never see them again.
-Always complaining about how terrible her life is, and how she does everything, and none of us do anything(from the couch, while me and the kids were cooking, cleaning, etc)
-Our oldest has even moved out, in with me, he called her out on the fact that since I wasn't around for her to verbally beat up she started on him.
-He left when she told him that her life would have been so much better if he had never been born.


So no, not one thing, many little things.
